summary: A Laracon EU 2019 conference talk by Antti Rössi titled "How your Laravel application can get hacked, and how to prevent that from happening".

title: Infinite Scale: Deploying and Scaling Laravel on Kubernetes
speaker: Leo Sjoberg
summary: The speaker demonstrates how to deploy and scale Laravel applications using Kubernetes, showing how it can help handle production deployments more smoothly and provide automatic scaling. Through a live demo, they show how to set up a basic Laravel deployment with nginx, FPM, and auto-scaling capabilities in just a few minutes using Kubernetes configuration files, emphasizing that no application code changes are needed.

title: Less Pain with Gain, how Laravel helps you scale your Applications
speaker: Martin Westphal
summary: A Laracon EU 2019 conference talk by Martin Westphal titled "Less Pain with Gain, how Laravel helps you scale your Applications".

title: Our Secret Project
speaker: Freek Van der Herten & Marcel Pociot
summary: The speakers present two new error handling tools for Laravel: Ignition and Flare. Ignition is a modern error page that will be the default in Laravel 6, offering improved error reporting with features like dark mode, blade template debugging, and runnable solutions. Flare is a new Laravel-specific error tracking service that integrates with Ignition, offering team collaboration features, notifications, and error sharing capabilities.

title: Performance optimization: how do I go about it?
speaker: Kasia Zien
summary: This talk focuses on performance optimization in PHP applications, covering why it matters, how to measure it, and various tools and techniques for identifying and fixing performance issues. The speaker shares practical examples using tools like Xdebug, XHProf, and flame graphs while emphasizing the importance of measuring before optimizing and maintaining a balance between performance and code readability.

title: Persuasive Design Patterns—Design experiences that enhance and align with motivations
speaker: Jenny Shen

title: SOLID in architecture
speaker: Michal Ksionek
summary: This talk discusses software architecture principles, focusing on SOLID principles at the component level. The speaker explains how to design and organize components, manage dependencies between them, and ensure good architectural practices. Key concepts covered include component cohesion rules (REP, CCP, CRP), component coupling principles (ADP, SDP, SAP), and how to measure and maintain stability and abstractness in software architecture.

title: The Art of Form Validation
speaker: Caneco
summary: This talk focuses on form validation best practices in Laravel and frontend frameworks, covering both client-side and server-side validation approaches. The speaker discusses various validation techniques including HTML5 validation, JavaScript libraries like V-validate, and Laravel's built-in validation features, while emphasizing the importance of creating user-friendly validation experiences across desktop and mobile devices.

title: The Beauty of Laravel's Notification System
speaker: Christoph Rumpel
summary: A comprehensive talk about Laravel's notification system delivered at Laracon, demonstrating how to implement different types of notifications including email, database, Slack, and real-time notifications using WebSockets. The speaker shows practical examples using Laravel Nova and demonstrates live notification broadcasting, concluding with implementing a Twitter notification integration.

title: Time Driven Development

summary: The talk introduces the concept of 'Time Driven Development' - a balanced approach to software development that considers both business value and code quality. The speaker shares experiences from real projects to illustrate when to invest time in architecture (using patterns like Repository and Factory) versus when to opt for simpler solutions. She emphasizes that software design principles should be treated as tools rather than goals, and developers should make pragmatic decisions based on project context and business value.

speaker: Marcus Moore
summary: Marcus Moore presents a talk about behavior-driven development (BDD) in Laravel, explaining how BDD helps bridge communication gaps between stakeholders and developers. speaker: Freek Van der Herten
summary: The talk discusses structuring large Laravel applications using domains and improving frontend interactions using TypeScript. The speaker shares examples from Flare, an exception tracking application, to demonstrate how to organize code into domains for better maintainability.

title: Crafting maintainable Laravel applications
speaker: Jason McCreary
summary: Jason McCreary presents 10 tips for creating maintainable Laravel applications based on his experience with Shift and 20 years of programming. He covers topics ranging from staying current with Laravel versions to proper testing practices, emphasizing code readability and framework conventions.

title: CSS Grid: What is this magic?!
speaker: Amy Kapernick
summary: This talk provides a comprehensive introduction to CSS Grid, covering its evolution from early web layouts through to modern implementation. The speaker demonstrates practical examples of building a note-taking app layout using CSS Grid, discusses browser support including IE compatibility issues, and shares various learning resources.

title: Expressive Eloquent collections
speaker: Tim MacDonald
summary: Tim McDonald discusses how to make Laravel Eloquent collections more expressive and maintainable. He explores how collections can be extended to better reflect domain language, reduce code duplication, and improve readability.

title: How to build an API in a day with Laravel API Boilerplate
speaker: Max Snow
summary: Max presents his Laravel API Boilerplate project, which helps developers quickly build REST APIs. The boilerplate provides out-of-the-box functionality for common API features like CRUD operations, transformers, authorization, and case conversion between snake\_case and camelCase.

title: Level up: The super dev
speaker: Patima Tantiprasut
summary: A talk about what makes a 'super developer', challenging common perceptions by arguing that the best developers are those who are 'slow' (thoughtful), 'selfish' (maintain work-life balance), 'lazy' (avoid repetitive code), like to argue (engage in healthy debate), and write 'bad' code (embrace imperfection and learning). The speaker emphasizes the importance of personal wellbeing, setting boundaries, and avoiding toxic hustle culture in development.

title: Making Single Page Apps accessible
speaker: Jess Budd
summary: The talk focuses on making single page applications more accessible, delivered by Jess, a front-end developer and accessibility consultant. She discusses key accessibility considerations including semantic HTML, form labeling, keyboard navigation, and focus management in React and Vue applications.

title: Managing a team building a modular monolith in Laravel
speaker: Stephen Rowe
summary: Steven, the head of development at Figured, discusses how his company builds a modular monolith using Laravel and manages self-organizing development pods. He explains their approach to maintaining code consistency while giving development teams autonomy, their package-based architecture, and how they enable quick deployment cycles while maintaining code quality.

title: Not a designer? You can make your website more accessible
speaker: Georgie Luhur Cooke
summary: A talk focusing on web accessibility and inclusive design principles. The speaker discusses how to make websites more accessible through proper typography, color contrast, semantic HTML, and interactive elements.

title: Package design 101
speaker: Marcel Pociot
summary: The talk demonstrates how to create and publish Laravel packages, walking through the creation of a badge/gamification package as an example. The speaker shows how to set up package boilerplate, create migrations, implement models and traits, set up testing with Orchestra TestBench, and create facades.

title: Reformat, Refactor, Replace: A practical guide for dealing with legacy software
speaker: Samuel Levy
summary: The speaker discusses strategies for modernizing and refactoring legacy PHP applications. He covers the challenges of dealing with old, poorly structured codebases and presents a methodical approach to upgrading them using the 'strangler fig' pattern.

title: Testing Javascript: Building JavaScript applications you won't hate
speaker: Michael Timbs
summary: A comprehensive talk about testing JavaScript and frontend applications, focusing on making testing more manageable and enjoyable. The speaker covers various testing tools and approaches, from static analysis to end-to-end testing, with practical examples of how to implement them effectively.

title: The Laravel developer's guide to Vue SPAs
speaker: Jess Archer
summary: Jess Archer shares her experience building a single page application (SPA) with Laravel and Vue.js, focusing on practical solutions to common challenges. She discusses authentication approaches, state management with Vuex, and frontend optimization techniques based on lessons learned while building Giftie Duck, a gift reminder service.

title: Types & static analysis are good in PHP
speaker: Sam Greenwood
summary: Sam Greenwood presents a comprehensive talk on the importance of types and static analysis in PHP and Laravel applications. He discusses different types of typing systems, the benefits of static analysis tools like PHPStan, Psalm, and Larastan, and how these tools can help improve code quality and catch potential errors before runtime, especially in legacy applications.

title: Zero Knowledge: you can't leak what you don't know
speaker: Ben Dechrai
summary: This talk discusses approaches to securing data and communications in software-as-a-service applications, particularly focusing on end-to-end encryption, zero-knowledge systems, and practical ways to protect user data. The speaker uses a banking/financial data example to illustrate concepts around encrypting sensitive information while still maintaining service functionality.

title: An Introduction to View Components in Laravel 7
speaker: Marcel Pociot
summary: Marcel Pociot presents a comprehensive overview of Laravel 7's new View Components feature. He demonstrates how to create and use class-based components, anonymous components, and inline components, showing various ways to pass data, handle attributes, and manage component rendering logic. The talk includes live coding examples of creating reusable UI components like sidebars, markdown renderers, and buttons.

speaker: Johannes Pichler
summary: A Laracon EU 2020 conference talk by Johannes Pichler titled "Battle Tested API Design".

title: Build Branding that doesn't suck
speaker: Caneco
summary: A presentation on creating effective brand designs for software projects, particularly in the Laravel ecosystem. The speaker, Kaneko, shares his experience designing logos for various Laravel projects and provides practical tips on brand identity, from logo design to merchandise creation. He emphasizes the importance of pixel-perfect exports, choosing appropriate colors, and maintaining brand consistency across different platforms.

title: Building a Realtime Dashboard Powered by Laravel and Livewire
speaker: Freek Van der Herten
summary: A presentation about building real-time dashboards using Laravel, Livewire, and the Laravel Dashboard package. The speaker demonstrates how to create dynamic dashboard tiles that auto-refresh and display various data sources like Google Calendar events and Twitter feeds. The talk includes live coding demonstrations and explains the underlying architecture of the dashboard package.

title: Building APIs with Laravel using OpenAPI
speaker: Chris Tankersley
summary: Chris Tankersley presents on using OpenAPI to document and build APIs in Laravel. He explains how OpenAPI serves as a specification format for HTTP APIs, demonstrates tools like Stoplight Studio for API design, and shows how to generate Laravel boilerplate code from OpenAPI specs. The talk focuses on practical implementation using a to-do app example while highlighting the benefits of consistent API documentation and development.

title: CSRF is dead
speaker: Stephen Rees-Carter
summary: A comprehensive talk about CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) attacks and Same-Site Cookies in Laravel applications. The speaker explains how CSRF attacks work, demonstrates different Same-Site Cookie attributes (Strict, Lax, None), and discusses how Laravel implements Same-Site Cookie protection. The talk includes live demonstrations and explains why CSRF protection remains important despite new browser security features.

title: Deploying Laravel with Ansible
speaker: Erika Heidi
summary: Erika Heidi presents a comprehensive talk on deploying Laravel applications using Ansible. The talk covers Ansible fundamentals, setting up playbooks, working with group variables, and securing sensitive data with Ansible Vault. The presentation includes a live demo of deploying a Laravel travel list application to multiple servers simultaneously using Ansible automation.

title: Laravel Secrets
speaker: Bobby Bouwmann
summary: The talk covers several Laravel secrets and internal workings, focusing on exception handling, model attributes/relationships, and event handling. The speaker demonstrates how Laravel's exception handler works, explains the order of operations for model attribute access, and shows how to leverage Laravel's command events system for adding custom output to artisan commands.

title: Nuno Maduro
speaker: Introducing Pest
summary: Nuno presents Pest, an elegant PHP testing framework built on top of PHPUnit. The talk demonstrates how Pest simplifies testing syntax, reduces boilerplate code, and provides a more user-friendly experience through features like higher-order tests, datasets, and improved test coverage reporting. The framework maintains compatibility with existing PHPUnit tests while offering a more modern and concise testing API.

title: PhpStorm, From a Fresh Install To A Master Laravel Setup
speaker: Christoph Rumpel
summary: A comprehensive tutorial on setting up and optimizing PHPStorm IDE for Laravel development. The talk focuses on improving developer productivity through proper IDE setup and useful features like the IDE Helper package for better Laravel integration.

The talk emphasizes Laravel's continued evolution toward a more streamlined, modern framework while maintaining backward compatibility.

title: Lessons From The Laravel Framework
speaker: Luke Downing
summary: A talk about learning important development lessons from Laravel's design choices. The speaker discusses how Laravel's ordinary and obvious approach leads to better developer experience, using examples like routing conventions and facades. He emphasizes how sometimes breaking traditional programming rules can be beneficial when the gains in developer productivity outweigh the theoretical drawbacks.

title: Let Rector do the Boring Work
speaker: Tomas Votruba
summary: Tomas Votruba shows how Rector automates PHP refactors and upgrades so developers spend less time on mechanical changes.

speaker: Christoph Rumpel

He discusses the challenges faced and solutions implemented, including parallel testing, optimizing setup methods, and dealing with caching issues, ultimately reducing the test runtime to 5 minutes.

title: Maximizing Your Team'S Performance
speaker: Katerina Trajchevska
summary: Kaarina discusses how to improve team performance and code quality, particularly when dealing with legacy code. She explores strategies for writing testable code, implementing proper design patterns, and making incremental improvements. The talk covers characterization testing for legacy code, using SOLID principles for new features, and techniques like sprouting and wrapping for extending legacy systems while maintaining code quality.

title: Parsing PHP For Fun...And Profit
speaker: Marcel Pociot
summary: This talk explores PHP parsing using the PHP-Parser library. The speaker demonstrates how to parse PHP code into an abstract syntax tree (AST), manipulate the AST, and transform it back into PHP code. Through practical examples, he shows how to modify strings, remove dump statements, and wrap echo statements in function calls - techniques that are used in tools like Laravel Tinker Well.

title: Real-Time Laravel
speaker: Joe Dixon
summary: Joe Dixon presents Laravel Reverb, a new websocket server for Laravel applications that enables real-time communication. The talk demonstrates how to implement real-time messaging, typing indicators, and presence detection using Reverb alongside Laravel's existing broadcasting capabilities. The presentation includes a live demonstration building a Slack-like chat interface and highlights Reverb's seamless integration with Laravel Forge and Pulse.

title: Reusing Reusable Livewire Components
speaker: Philo
summary: The talk covers creating reusable Livewire components in Laravel, focusing on building a dynamic modal system. The speaker demonstrates how to create interactive UI components using Livewire 3 and Alpine.js, including lazy loading, event handling, and state management. He showcases practical examples through building a login modal and discusses his experience creating Wire Elements, a component library for Livewire.

title: Running Laravel Apps With FrankenPHP
speaker: Kévin Dunglas
summary: Kevin Dunglas introduces FrankenPHP, a modern PHP application server that replaces traditional PHP-FPM/Apache setups. He explains how FrankenPHP simplifies deployment, improves performance through Laravel Octane integration, and offers features like HTTP/3 support and built-in Mercure for real-time capabilities. The talk covers both basic usage and advanced features like packaging PHP applications as standalone binaries.

title: Scaling Databases
speaker: Tobias Petry
summary: Tobias Petri discusses database scaling strategies in Laravel applications, focusing on the progression from single server to read replication to sharding. He emphasizes the importance of optimizing existing setups before moving to more complex solutions, warns about common pitfalls in each scaling approach, and explains how different scaling solutions fit different application needs. The talk includes practical examples using a hypothetical Laravel e-commerce platform selling conference tickets.

title: Surviving Large Applications
speaker: Bobby Bouwmann
summary: Bobby Balman from Hospitable discusses strategies for maintaining and surviving large Laravel applications. He shares experiences from managing a large-scale Laravel application processing 51 million jobs daily, emphasizing the importance of consistent code structure, proper testing, and following Laravel defaults. The talk focuses on practical approaches to organizing code in domains/modules while keeping things simple and maintainable.

title: The PHP Foundation
speaker: Roman Pronskiy
summary: The talk discusses the PHP Foundation, its creation, and its role in supporting PHP development. The speaker explains how PHP went from having only 2 paid developers in 2021 to establishing a foundation that now supports 10+ developers. The talk covers the foundation's mission, current projects, funding model, and future roadmap for PHP development.

title: Thoughtful Performance
speaker: Tim
summary: A talk focused on thoughtful performance optimization in Laravel applications, covering strategies for concurrent operations, cache management, and rate limiting. The speaker discusses various techniques including HTTP request pooling, process concurrency, cache warming strategies, and implementing rate limits to ensure fair resource distribution among users.

title: Uncharted Packages
speaker: Freek Van der Herten
summary: Freek Van der Herten presents his 10th consecutive Laracon talk, showcasing 10 lesser-known but useful Laravel packages from Spatie's collection of over 300 packages. He demonstrates practical applications of packages including Laravel Horizon Watcher, Laravel Remote, Support Bubble, Slack Alerts, Query Builder, Login Link, Laravel Steps, Blade Comments, Laravel PDF, and Schedule Monitor. The talk highlights how these packages solve common development challenges and improve developer experience.

title: Unveiling The Modular Monolith
speaker: Mateus
summary: This talk covers modular monoliths as an architectural approach for Laravel applications. The speaker discusses how to organize code into modules while maintaining the benefits of a monolithic application, exploring concepts like boundary definition, inter-module communication through events, and data ownership. He contrasts this with both traditional monoliths and microservices, explaining how modular monoliths can provide a middle ground that offers better code organization and team independence while avoiding the complexity of distributed systems.

title: Window Magic, Command Line Wizardry
speaker: Rissa Jackson
summary: Marissa Jackson presents a comprehensive talk on command line tools and window management for developers, focusing on improving workflow efficiency. She demonstrates various tools including Hammerspoon for window management, Oh My Zsh for terminal customization, and Raycast for productivity. The presentation includes live demos of snippets, quick links, and clipboard management, with particular emphasis on making development workflows more efficient and enjoyable.

title: Working At Laravel
speaker: James Brooks

The talk covers their tools and workflows, including their use of GitHub, Basecamp, Slack, and Help Scout. James also demonstrates a technical example of how they improved Forge's provisioning system.

title: Advanced HTML for good developers
speaker: Mandy Michael

The speaker emphasizes the importance of using semantic HTML elements correctly instead of generic div elements, explains how HTML impacts the DOM and accessibility tree, and covers various HTML attributes and resource hints that can optimize page loading.

title: Legacy to Laravel in 30 minutes
speaker: Jordan Havard
summary: Jordan shares how his team turned a decade old multi tenant PHP beast into a modern Laravel application without stopping the business. From six tangled repositories and a single method Lumen API to a fully tested Laravel platform, he shows the patterns, tools and tests that made a safe migration possible.

title: Markup matters
speaker: Charlie Morris
summary: Charlie Morris shows how semantic HTML underpins every accessible and consistent user experience on the web. With clear demonstrations using screen readers, voice control and the browser’s accessibility tree, she reveals how small markup decisions in Laravel apps either empower or exclude users.

title: Mid-life Composer
speaker: Ryan Lovett
summary: Ryan closes Laracon AU with a powerful and vulnerable story about identity, burnout, and rebuilding after major life change. This talk explores mental health, psychology, and what it really means to define yourself beyond your job title.

title: No dev. No staging. No problem.
speaker: James Mooring
summary: James Mooring shares how Astalty ships straight to production with trunk-based development, simple infrastructure, and a strong engineering quality bar. He breaks down the practices that make it safe, then demos a live production merge and feature-flag rollout on stage.

title: React, the Laravel way
speaker: Simon Vrachliotis
summary: Simon shares how Laravel and Inertia transformed his ability to ship full stack React projects after years of JavaScript ecosystem fatigue. He walks through the ergonomics of JSX, the overwhelm of modern tooling, and the moment Laravel’s batteries included philosophy unlocked a simpler, more joyful workflow.

title: Ship faster with Blueprint
speaker: Jason McCreary
summary: See how Jason McCreary’s Blueprint turns a tiny YAML “draft” into full Laravel scaffolding - models, migrations, controllers, views, and even realistic tests – so you can move from laravel new to a working app in minutes. He demos Blueprint’s conventions, shorthands, configuration, and support for existing projects, then shows how it fits alongside AI and Boost to help you ship Laravel applications faster and with confidence.

title: Small steps, Big shifts
speaker: Michael Dyrynda
summary: Laracon AU 2025 opens with an energetic, cinematic intro and a heartfelt keynote inviting developers to “Level Up” through community, curiosity, and shared passion. The talk reflects on the evolution of PHP and Laravel, the power of human creativity in an AI-augmented world, and the importance of belonging and connection over the next two days.

title: UI details that connect
speaker: Leah Thompson
summary: Leah Thompson from the Laravel DevRel team shows how to approach front-end development without fear by breaking designs into simple, repeatable steps. Through live demos of real Laravel sites, she demonstrates how spacing, typography, layering, and interaction can turn plain layouts into polished experiences.

title: Writing resilient code
speaker: Zuzana Kunckova
summary: Zuzana explores what it means to write resilient Laravel applications that keep working under stress, from traffic spikes and flaky networks to failing third party APIs. She walks through practical techniques including robust input validation, safer error handling, monitoring and logging, retries, graceful degradation and testing beyond the happy path so your users and future self are not blindsided when things go wrong.

title: A Fresh Start(er) for Laravel
speaker: Josh Cirre
summary: Ready to level up your Laravel workflow from the very first command? Whether you're a long-time Laravel developer or just getting started, Josh brings fresh perspective, real-world guidance, and hands-on insight into how modern Laravel development is evolving.

title: A Slice of Pi
speaker: Dan Johnson
summary: What happens when software engineering meets hardware tinkering? 🍰 At Laracon India 2025, Dan Johnson, Head of Engineering at Trybe, takes the stage with an inspiring and curious talk titled "A Slice of Pi." Known for building innovative solutions in the hotel spa industry and a passion for hardware experimentation, Dan blends his technical expertise with a maker’s mindset to deliver something truly unique.

title: Advanced Image Processing with PHP
speaker: Mathias Grimm
summary: Join Mathias Grimm, an Engineer at Laravel and founder of a cutting-edge B2B SaaS platform, as he takes us through an exciting journey of building a robust Image Processing Service with PHP & Laravel during Laracon India 2025. Whether you're a seasoned developer or just getting started with PHP Laravel, this talk is packed with actionable takeaways that will level up your skills.

title: Async PHP with Coroutines: Building Scalable Apps
speaker: Khushboo Verma
summary: At Laracon India 2025, Khushboo Verma - Platform Engineer at Appwrite, Docker Captain, and renowned tech speaker - presented a forward-looking session titled "Async PHP with Coroutines: Building Scalable Applications". In this talk, Khushboo dives into the world of Async PHP with Coroutines, revealing how modern approaches can drastically improve the way PHP applications are built and scaled.

title: Beyond the Framework - Value Creation Development
speaker: Vatsal Shah
summary: At Laracon India 2025, renowned business catalyst and global speaker Vatsal Shah takes the stage with a transformative talk: "Beyond the Framework: Focusing on Value Creation and Customer-Centric Development." In this powerful session, Vatsal challenges developers and tech leaders to shift their perspective - from building features to delivering real-world impact. He shares actionable insights on aligning your development process with customer needs, driving business outcomes, and building products that truly matter.

title: Filament PHP Deep Dive: Build Faster, Smarter
speaker: Lucas Giovanny
summary: Looking to master Filament PHP and take your Laravel filament experience to the next level? Join Lucas Giovanny, Engineering Team Lead and prolific Open Source Contributor, as he takes the Laracon India 2025 stage with his session: "Dive Deep into Filament PHP." This isn't just an introduction - it's a hands-on, high-impact session packed with performance tips, power features, and speed hacks that will change the way you build admin panels in Laravel.

title: Frustrated Bob
speaker: Bert De Swaef
summary: Bert De Swaef is a developer and Founder at Vulpo Digital Studio. He loves to create YouTube Tutorials for fellow Developers.

title: Generative AI and LLM in PHP
speaker: Ashish Tiwari
summary: At Laracon India 2025, Ashish Tiwari — Senior Developer Advocate at Elastic and Search Engineer — presented an eye-opening talk on "Generative AI and Large Language Model (LLM) in PHP." With deep expertise in AI, search technologies, and developer advocacy, Ashish brings a practical, forward-thinking approach to integrating advanced AI capabilities into your PHP applications. In this talk, he explores how LLMs are reshaping the developer landscape, from intelligent code generation and content creation to smarter search experiences and automation..

title: Go for PHP Developers
speaker: Michi Hoffmann
summary: At Laracon India 2025, Michi Hoffmann - Senior Software Engineer at Sentry and Laracon speaker across the globe - shared a powerful session titled "Go for PHP Developers." This talk is designed to help Laravel and PHP developers broaden their development horizons.

title: Implementing Multitenancy in Laravel
speaker: Freek Van der Herten
summary: Freek Van der Herten is a partner at Spatie and a Laravel expert known for building powerful open-source packages. During Laracon India 2025, he shared insights on implementing multitenancy in Laravel, helping developers scale their applications efficiently.

title: Laravel Kubernetes and You!
speaker: Justin Reasoner
summary: Get ready to explore the future of infrastructure with Justin Reasoner, He is Infra Engineer at Laravel. 🚀 During Laracon India 2025 talk, Justin dives deep into Laravel, Kubernetes, and YOU - yes, you!

title: Modern PHP Tooling
speaker: Nuno Maduro
summary: Get ready for an insightful session on modern PHP tooling with Nuno Maduro at Laracon India 2025! Nuno, a core member of Laravel and many other amazing platform, takes us through the latest advancements in PHP tooling.

title: Modularizing Inertia
speaker: Ryuta Hamasaki
summary: Ready to scale your Inertia.js application the smart way? At Laracon India 2025, Ryuta Hamasaki, Developer at Laravel and member of the NightWatch team, takes the spotlight with his session: "Modularizing Inertia." This talk dives deep into scalable frontend architecture using Inertia.js seamless experience.

title: Supercharge Your Laravel App with LLM
speaker: Pushpak Chhajed
summary: What happens when you combine the elegance of Laravel with the intelligence of Large Language Models (LLMs)? You get the future of smart, dynamic applications - and it’s closer than you think.

title: The Secret to Developer Happiness
speaker: Dave Hicking
summary: At Laracon India 2025, Dave Hicking - Product Manager at LaraJobs and HelpSpot — delivered a thoughtful session, "The Secret to Developer Happiness." Drawing from years of experience working closely with developers and product teams, Dave shares powerful insights into what makes developers feel valued, productive, and inspired. It explores the human side of software development, covering team dynamics, communication, career growth, and the mindset needed to build not just great products, but meaningful, sustainable careers in tech.

title: Unlikely Coder
speaker: Nina Karisik
summary: Not every coder follows the traditional path — and that's exactly what makes their journey powerful. At Laracon India 2025, Nina Karisik, Software Engineer and advocate for diversity in tech, talk about story in "Unlikely Coder." Through her inspiring talk, Nina encourages developers from all backgrounds to embrace their unique stories and find their place in tech.

title: "Ship or Die" Closing Panel and Pitch Competition
speaker: Taylor Otwell, Adam Wathan, Thorsten Ball, Hannah Gzehoviak
summary: Seven community members, three minutes each, and then hands off the keyboard. Pitch your startup, side project, or art project to Taylor Otwell, Adam Wathan, Thorsten Ball, and Hannah Gzehoviak, Shark Tank style.

title: AI Can Do Your Job... What Now?
speaker: Will King
summary: If you can describe what done looks like before the work starts, AI can do it, and it should. What's left is the creative work of figuring out what's worth building, and creativity isn't a gift you either have or don't.

title: Building a CLI Coding Agent from Scratch
speaker: Mateus Guimarães
summary: The model is the raw intelligence, and the harness is the product. Claude Code and Codex run the same models everyone else has, so what differs is context assembly, the tool registry, authorization, sandboxing, compaction, and session state.

title: Building a Video Processing Pipeline with Laravel Queues
speaker: Joshua Alphonse
summary: A user sees one action, but your system sees an entire workflow. The request records the work and leaves, the database remembers where it is, the queue keeps it moving, workers do the risky parts, and the UI just watches for state changes.

title: Building for Agents & Humans
speaker: Gordon Diggs
summary: Building well for agents turns out to be building well for people, and almost every decision that made Stripe Projects work for agents was already a decades-old best practice. Markdown documentation renders identically for both audiences, so there's no reason to write a separate LLM version.

title: Building Realtime Collaborative Apps with Laravel
speaker: Joe Tannenbaum
summary: Real time in Laravel starts with one command: php artisan install:broadcasting wires up both the server and client side and leaves you ready to broadcast. Presence channels tell you who's here, private channels gate access with a boolean, and whispers skip the app server entirely to go client to client through the websocket.

title: Building Software at the Edge of Your Understanding
speaker: Matt Stauffer
summary: AI lets you build things you don't understand, and the gap between what your app can do and what you actually know about it is comprehension debt. Like any debt, someone eventually pays it.

title: Cleverness is a Loan
speaker: Mary Perry
summary: Clever code is a loan taken against other people's time, and the interest rate is set by how many people have to service it. A seam is a place where you can change a program's behavior without editing it there, and Laravel is best understood as a collection of seams you can hand your complexity to.

title: Everything New with Laravel and Cloud
speaker: Taylor Otwell
summary: Laravel framework installs are past 350,000 a day, and the number of new Laravel apps created by coding agents is doubling roughly every five weeks. Shipping on the open source side: conditional container bindings through attributes, debounced jobs, a php artisan dev command that packages can register into, refreshable locks, first-party image manipulation, CPX 2.0, Pint for Blade, the new Laravel Head package, Str::summarize(), Inertia Chrome DevTools, an OpenAI-compatible AI SDK provider that unlocks local…

title: Filament: Advanced Practical Examples
speaker: Povilas Korop
summary: Filament isn't just an admin panel builder, it's an app builder, and thirteen real demos make the case.Attendance grids of checkboxes, colorful availability tables, GitHub-style contribution heat maps, tables rendered as grids instead of rows Roughly a hundred render hooks let you move the search bar to the other side or drop a user avatar above the sidebar, and a fully custom theme is possible if you're willing to write a lot of CSS to get there. Repeaters handle parent/child forms, while sections, tabs, and…

title: From Vibe Coding to Vibe Engineering
speaker: Kitze
summary: Kitze traces the last three years of AI-assisted development from vibe coding to what he calls vibe engineering. What does it look like to use agents for everything while staying permanently suspicious of what they produce.

title: Git, But Better: An Introduction to JJ
speaker: Pauline Vos
summary: Atomic commits, small logical changesets rather than chronological checkpoints, make code review reviewable commit by commit, eliminate the same merge conflict showing up over and over, and unlock features most people never touch, like bisect. They matter more with agents rather than less, because a clean log tells your agent what changed, why, and what's safe to revert when things run amok.

title: Introducing Pest 5
speaker: Nuno Maduro
summary: Nuno Maduro unveils Pest 5 with live demos of six new features: an agent plugin that lets Claude Code arrange a scenario, drive a browser, and make backend assertions in a single tool call; a PHPStan plugin for fully type-safe tests; a Rector plugin that rewrites AI-generated tests into idiomatic Pest; an evals plugin for testing AI agents against reference answers; time-based CI sharding so every shard finishes together; and the TIA engine, which cuts Laravel Cloud's local suite from 200 seconds to 5. Pest 5…

title: Laravel Community Update
speaker: Josh Cirre, Leah Thompson
summary: The only reason any of this happens is the community, so here's what it did this year: 1,776 pull requests merged into the framework and another 3,242 across the other repositories, over 5,000 in total, including 270 people contributing for the very first time. New starter kits shipped, including Svelte and a package skeleton that landed only weeks ago and is already being used.

title: Laravel is for the Builders
speaker: Aaron Francis
summary: Aaron Francis opens Laracon US 2026 by announcing his first day as Laravel's VP of Marketing and Community, then makes the case for why this is Laravel's moment. Small teams are outshipping big teams and individuals are outshipping companies, and the framework's 15-year history of craftsmanship has produced the most cohesive foundation to build on, from local development through deploying and scaling on Cloud.

title: Proven Package Patterns
speaker: Freek Van der Herten
summary: In the age of AI, packages still earn their place for hard problems, external problems, and tasteful solutions, but maybe not for the trivial shared ones an agent can write inline for your project. Keeping a package flexible without drowning in configuration comes down to a handful of patterns: fire events so users can hook in wherever they want instead of adding an option for every hook, let people register their own models and jobs by extending yours, and wrap low-level behavior in action classes they can…

title: Scaling Laravel
speaker: Devon Garbalosa
summary: Scaling a Laravel app isn't one decision or one vendor, it's chasing the fix to whichever layer it actually lives in. Sport Monks, running a thousand API requests and 24,000 database queries per second, had 75% of its database CPU going to a single unindexed query on the failed_jobs table.

title: The Desired State
speaker: Chris Fidao
summary: Building a cloud from a blank canvas starts with a few broad strokes that give you useful constraints: AWS, serverful, Kubernetes. After that it's all reconciliation.

title: The Last Software Engineer
speaker: Kent C. Dodds
summary: Agents are steadily taking over implementation work, and the slice left for us keeps shrinking, so the useful question is what the last valuable skill is before the end. The answer is judgment.

title: Think Harder: How I Prompt
speaker: Thorsten Ball
summary: Amp (ampcode.com) is 99% written by AI, and there's no secret sauce behind it: no MCP servers, no frameworks, no custom slash commands. There's one question, asked constantly.

title: Whimsy-Driven Development
speaker: Christina Martinez
summary: You have an inner Tamagotchi, and it will wither if you don't feed it. What feeds it is silly software.

title: Against all odds: NativePHP for mobile one year later
speaker: Simon Hamp
summary: Simon Hamp updates NativePHP for mobile a year on, covering bundle-size improvements, Android support, and continued work on shipping PHP-powered native apps.

title: AI won't fail loudly — It'll fail quietly
speaker: Yannick Kupferschmidt
summary: Yannick Kupferschmidt argues that AI agents fail through subtle bugs and architecture drift, and that the antidote is context engineering rather than larger context windows.

title: Building applications like Puzzles
speaker: Wendell Adriel
summary: Wendell Adriel discusses composing applications from interlocking pieces rather than treating the codebase as a single block.

title: Composer Deep Dive
speaker: Nils Adermann
summary: Nils Adermann, Composer's creator, gives a deep dive into Composer package management.

title: Effective Code Reviews: What NOT to Do
speaker: Luke Kuzmish
summary: Luke Kuzmish argues for taking ego out of code review: standardize the process, automate linting, review your own PR first, and use Conventional Comments.

title: Handling the unhappy path
speaker: Ryan Chandler
summary: Ryan Chandler highlights lesser-known Laravel features for dealing with errors and edge cases, including report() and response() on custom exceptions.

title: How real-world UX helps your projects thrive
speaker: Pete Heslop
summary: Pete Heslop draws on hospitals, restaurants, and airports to argue that good UX treats users like guests, reduces friction, and plans for mistakes.

title: Imports, a war story
speaker: Daniel Coulbourne
summary: Daniel Coulbourne shares the scars of migrating massive datasets and the import logic that has to survive real-world data.

title: Laravel Update
speaker: Taylor Otwell
summary: Taylor Otwell's Day 1 keynote recaps Laravel 13 (PHP 8.3+, attributes, Reverb database driver, passkeys, AI SDK) and demos an AI agent fixing a Nightwatch-detected bug live.

title: One billion rows with Laravel
speaker: Tobias Petry
summary: Tobias Petry covers querying and aggregating huge datasets with Laravel, including TimescaleDB/PostgreSQL aggregates for precomputing timeseries events.

title: Refactoring to Parallel
speaker: Marcel Pociot
summary: Marcel Pociot covers asynchronous refactoring patterns and concurrency for Laravel workloads, including AI pipelines.

title: Ship to Production on DAY 1
speaker: John Drexler
summary: John Drexler argues for solving the hardest problems first and shipping behind flags, using a Laravel Forge organizations migration and the strangler pattern as examples.

title: State of the Frontend
speaker: Joe Tannenbaum
summary: Joe Tannenbaum updates Laravel's frontend tooling and previews Inertia features coming in the next major version.

title: Things you didn't know you could do in CSS
speaker: Leah Thompson
summary: Leah Thompson presents CSS techniques that many backend-focused Laravel developers have not used yet.

title: This shouldn't work
speaker: Shane Rosenthal
summary: Shane Rosenthal of NativePHP shows how the project now generates real native C and renders native iOS and Android UI elements.

title: Unblocking your users with AI
speaker: Peter Suhm
summary: Peter Suhm of Tailwind Labs presents a practical framework for using AI at three user paralysis points—the blank state, the T-junction, and the maze—without replacing the product UI.

title: Write better abstractions: lessons from an import system
speaker: Dan Harrin
summary: Dan Harrin walks through how Filament decides what to abstract, arguing for description over instruction when designing reusable systems such as an import pipeline.

title: 10 Years of Laravel Content - What I Have Learned
speaker: Povilas Korop
summary: Povilas Korop, creator of Laravel Daily and one of the most recognized voices in the Laravel community, shares insights shaped by over a decade of teaching and creating content for developers worldwide. With years of experience helping developers grow, this session brings a rare perspective on learning, building, and evolving in the Laravel ecosystem.

title: Advanced Circuit Breakers for Laravel
speaker: Harris Raftopoulos
summary: Harris Raftopoulos, Staff & Educator at Laravel News and co-organizer of Laravel Greece Meetup, shares insights shaped by real-world experience in the Laravel ecosystem. Whether you're building resilient systems or exploring advanced patterns, this session brings a perspective that challenges how you think about reliability in Laravel.

title: Building Native Components with PHP
speaker: Simon Hamp & Shane Rosenthal
summary: Simon Hamp and Shane Rosenthal, the minds behind NativePHP, share insights from pushing the boundaries of what PHP can do beyond the browser. With a vision to bring PHP into native application development, this session delivers a fresh perspective on building modern experiences in unexpected ways.

title: Docker and Laravel - Optimize PHP with Docker
speaker: Francesco Ciulla
summary: Francesco Ciulla, Rust Educator, Docker Captain, international speaker, and DevOps enthusiast, shares insights shaped by working across modern cloud and scalable development environments.

title: Generics in PHP: Strong Typing with PHPDocs
speaker: Lucas Giovanny
summary: Lucas Giovanny, Engineering Lead at Worksome and open-source contributor, shares insights from his deep passion for PHP and modern web development. As PHP continues to evolve, this session brings a fresh perspective on writing more structured and reliable code.

title: Inside Nightwatch: Real-Time Analytics at Scale
speaker: Jess Archer
summary: Jess Archer, Engineering Team Lead at Laravel building Nightwatch, shares insights from working on real-time analytics at scale within the Laravel ecosystem. From handling complexity to delivering performance at scale, this session offers a unique inside look at what it takes to power modern developer tools.

title: Laravel + Vector Databases: Real-World AI Workloads
speaker: Chirag Daxini
summary: Chirag Daxini, Technical Project Manager with 11+ years of experience, brings a practical, execution-driven perspective on building real-world solutions with modern technologies. As AI moves from hype to real implementation, this session highlights what it actually takes to turn ideas into scalable, impactful systems.

title: Laravel AI SDK
speaker: Taylor Otwell
summary: Taylor Otwell, creator of Laravel, takes the stage to share what's next for the framework that powers millions of applications worldwide - Laravel AI SDK. As Laravel continues to evolve, this moment marks a new chapter - shaping how developers will build in the years ahead.

title: Live Coding Music with PHP
speaker: Marcel Pociot
summary: Marcel Pociot, CTO at Beyond Code and creator of tools like Laravel Herd, Tinkerwell, and Expose, brings a completely different perspective to what’s possible with PHP. Pushing beyond traditional boundaries, this session showcases creativity in a way that redefines how we think about the Laravel ecosystem.

title: Next-Gen Laravel DevOps with AI
speaker: Neel Shah
summary: Neel Shah, former Developer Advocate at Middleware and co-organiser of Open Source Weekend, shares insights from working at the intersection of DevOps, AI, and modern Laravel development. As development workflows evolve rapidly, this session brings a fresh perspective on how developers can adapt and stay ahead.

title: Proven Package Patterns
speaker: Freek Van der Herten
summary: Freek is a core contributor in the Laravel ecosystem and creator of hundreds of open-source packages, Freek brings real-world insights into designing packages that are clean, scalable, and built to last. Whether you're building your first package or maintaining widely-used libraries, this talk will help you level up your approach with practical strategies and proven structures.

title: Realtime Matters Until it Doesn't
speaker: Bert De Swaef
summary: Bert De Swaef, developer at Vulpoweb, YouTuber, and public speaker, shares insights shaped by his experience in PHP and Laravel. As modern applications push towards real-time everything, this session brings a perspective that challenges how and when it truly matters.

title: Refactor the Resistance
speaker: Hetal Mistry
summary: Hetal Mistry, Director of Global Delivery and agile leader, shares insights shaped by leading teams, managing complex projects, and driving continuous improvement across organizations. In a world where change is constant, this session brings a powerful perspective on navigating resistance and building stronger, outcome-driven teams.

title: Scaling Laravel for Millions of Products: Lessons from Bagisto
speaker: Devansh Bawari
summary: Devansh Bawari, Assistant Vice President at Webkul and a key contributor to the Bagisto ecosystem, shares insights from building large-scale, performance-driven e-commerce systems. As applications grow in scale and complexity, this session brings a real-world perspective on what it takes to build systems that truly hold up.

title: Staying Productive in PHP with Livewire
speaker: Jigar Dhulla
summary: Jigar Dhulla, Software Engineer with 15+ years of experience and a leading voice in the Indian Laravel community, shares insights shaped by building scalable web applications. As development demands speed and efficiency, this session brings a practical perspective on staying productive while building modern PHP applications.

title: Strict AI Engineering
speaker: Nuno Maduro
summary: Nuno Maduro, Staff Software Engineer at Laravel and creator of tools like Pest, Pint, and Larastan, shares insights shaped by building tools used by millions of developers worldwide. As AI becomes part of everyday development, this session brings a disciplined perspective on how to build systems that are not just powerful — but reliable and structured.

title: Tailwind Utilities You Didn't Know You Needed
speaker: Shruti Balasa
summary: Shruti Balasa, full-stack developer, educator, and Laravel community contributor, shares insights from her experience simplifying web development for thousands of learners. Known for making complex concepts easy, this session brings a fresh perspective that can change how you approach building modern UIs.

title: Write Code That Can Fix Itself
speaker: Punyapal Shah
summary: Punyapal Shah, Laravel Artisan, open-source contributor, and founder of the Laravel Artisans community, shares insights shaped by building robust and scalable applications - RectorPHP. As codebases grow and complexity increases, this session brings a forward-thinking perspective on writing code that evolves with you.
